1	// Shared-mmap allocation for andesim.
2	//
3	// The caller asks for `size` bytes; we resolve a backing directory over a
4	// tier list (first fit wins, fit = size + 256 MiB free), allocate a sparse
5	// file with mkstemp+truncate, and print one status line that always names
6	// the chosen tier -- and, when we fell past /dev/shm, why. HSIM_MMAP_DIR
7	// pins a single tier (hard error if it does not fit; no fallback past it).

20	// One backing-store candidate: the directory plus the label used in
21	// status/error messages ("/dev/shm", "~/.cache/andesim", "HSIM_MMAP_DIR=..").
22	struct MmapTier {
23	  std::string dir;
24	  std::string label;
25	};

28	// was skipped, a human note saying which and why ("" when tiers[0] fit).

30	  std::string dir;
31	  std::string note;

36	// to the argparse-style message. Fractional values truncate (1.5G -> whole
37	// bytes).

39	
40	// L26/F2: the physical shared mmap is one V-scratch page (HYBRID_V_SCRATCH_BYTES)
41	// larger than the program's --mem-size, so the V-register transport page sits
42	// just ABOVE the program's declared RAM. No program layout -- low stack, top-of-
43	// RAM stack, or a heap grown to the ceiling -- can reach a page past its own
44	// RAM, so the scratch can never be clobbered. The vsim side parks the scratch
45	// at the mmap's top page (v_scratch_gpa), which equals ram_base + program_bytes.
46	long long physical_mmap_bytes(long long program_bytes);

68	//   else            -> /dev/shm, then $XDG_CACHE_HOME|~/.cache + /andesim

5	// engines whose content or device behavior the handoff actually provides.

7	// and unverified-parity devices (UART1/SMU) are deliberately absent.

11	//     reserved HYBRID_V_SCRATCH_BYTES page above program RAM, L26).

1	// The phase-plan grammar driven by run_plan (F6), minus the dropped QEMU2
2	// step.
3	//
4	// A Plan is a list of Steps; each Step names an engine (by id, resolved against
5	// the F2 registry), the role to invoke it in (its `invoke` template key, e.g.
6	// "fast-leg" / "accurate-leg"), and a Trigger. run_plan spawns each leg in
7	// order, threads the drained hybrid_state_v1 file forward, and returns each
8	// leg's mcycle/minstret. Under the no-QEMU2-handback design every F6 step
9	// drains, so the hybrid cycle figure is the vsim-leg mcycle minus the qemu-leg
10	// mcycle.
11	#ifndef ANDESIM_PLAN_HPP
12	#define ANDESIM_PLAN_HPP
13	
14	#include <map>
15	#include <string>
16	#include <vector>
17	
18	#include "hybrid/state_abi.h"
19	
20	namespace andes_sim {
21	
22	// The ROI delimiter for a step. `kind` is marker|pc; `params` carries
23	// kind-specific values (e.g. enter_pc, exit_pc) that F9 maps onto trigger
24	// args. F6 only exercises the default marker case (no params).
25	struct Trigger {
26	  std::string kind;
27	  std::map<std::string, std::string> params;
28	};
29	
30	// One leg of a plan: which engine, which invoke role, under which trigger.
31	// `extra_args` are verbatim tokens appended after the filled template and the
32	// trigger args -- the seam for user-forwarded per-leg flags (e.g. the vsim
33	// leg's --kanata), which are orthogonal to the trigger.
34	struct Step {
35	  std::string engine_id;  // "qemu" | "verilator:ax45mpv_premium"
36	  std::string role;       // invoke-template key: "fast-leg" | "accurate-leg"
37	  Trigger trigger;
38	  std::vector<std::string> extra_args{};  // default-init: keeps 3-field Step{} literals warning-free
39	};

41	// A whole hybrid run. Every step loads `elf`; the shared mmap (`mem_size`
42	// bytes, at `mmap_path` or allocated by run_plan when empty) survives across
43	// every leg so memory threads through.
44	struct Plan {
45	  std::string elf;          // path to the ELF every leg launches
46	  long long mem_size = 0;   // shared-mmap size in bytes
47	  std::string mmap_path;    // "" => run_plan allocates one (F5) and owns it
48	  std::vector<Step> steps;

58	// rides the engine's stdout and must flow through to the user. `st` is the
59	// full drained record (verify_oracle F4: run --verify diffs the vsim drain
60	// against the oracle leg's in-process, after run_plan removed the files).
61	struct PhaseResult {
62	  unsigned long long mcycle = 0;
63	  unsigned long long minstret = 0;
64	  std::string out;
65	  hybrid_state_v1 st{};
66	};

72	  std::vector<PhaseResult> phases;

13	// first `--` is captured verbatim into `passthrough` and is NOT interpreted by
14	// the framework. That is what lets `fast`/`cycle` forward an engine's whole

27	// dispatch.

32	  std::string model;                      // --mode fast|cycle|hybrid (field stays 'model': the concept, see list models)
33	  std::string engine;                     // --engine <id>
34	  std::string trigger;                    // --trigger marker|pc
35	  // Hybrid trigger args (empty => cmd_run applies the default). pc boundaries
36	  // are a symbol name or 0x address; the sizes stay strings here and are
37	  // parsed where they are used.
38	  std::string pc_start;                   // --pc-start (trigger pc)
39	  std::string pc_end;                     // --pc-end   (trigger pc)
40	  std::string mem_size;                   // --mem-size (guest memory; --mmap-size is a hidden alias)
41	  std::string runtime;                    // --runtime linux (proxy-kernel payload; "" => bare-metal ELF, the default)
42	  std::string kanata;                     // --kanata <file> (marker/pc ROI trace)
43	  std::string objdump;                    // --objdump <file> (kanata labels)
44	  std::string log_level;                  // --log-level 0..6 (vsim scale; "" => info)

findings.title: --print-memmap 'OVERLAPS the reserved V-scratch page' branch is unreachable
findings.detail: In run_hybrid, the L26/F3 overlap guard (cmd_run.cpp:468-483) runs unconditionally, including in memmap_only mode: it computes scratch_gpa = physical_mmap_bytes(mem) - HYBRID_V_SCRATCH_BYTES, which equals mem exactly (shm.cpp:87-89 defines physical_mmap_bytes as program_bytes + HYBRID_V_SCRATCH_BYTES), and returns fail() when elf_load_top(elf_path) > scratch_gpa. The --print-memmap block at lines 504-532 executes only after that guard passed, and calls the same deterministic elf_load_top on the same elf_path, so at line 526 'top <= mem' is always true and the else-branch string 'OVERLAPS the reserved V-scratch page; raise --mem-size' (lines 528-529) can never print. Note the design tension: the comment at lines 403-406 says the ELF 'only adds the fit-vs-scratch note' in memmap mode, but the hard guard fires first - if the OVERLAPS note was meant to be reachable under --print-memmap, the guard would need a memmap_only skip (a behavioral choice, out of structural scope).
findings.safety: Removing the unreachable ternary else-branch (leaving the unconditional 'fits DRAM' note, or hoisting the guard result) cannot change any observable output, because no input reaches that branch: any ELF with top > mem already exited with the fail() diagnostic before the memmap block runs.
findings.verify_with: tests/andes_sim/test_andes_sim_print_memmap.sh (asserts the map output and gating) plus a manual `./andesim run --mode hybrid --print-memmap` with an oversized ELF showing the fail() path fires first, before and after the change.

findings.title: spawn_inherit's stdin_from_devnull parameter is never true - the /dev/null branch is dead
findings.detail: spawn_inherit (process.cpp:48-68, anonymous namespace, so no external callers) takes bool stdin_from_devnull and, when true, redirects the child's stdin from /dev/null (lines 56-62). Its only two callers both pass false: exec_passthrough (line 154, /*stdin_from_devnull=*/false) and fork_background (line 158, same). Grep over driver/ confirms no other call site. The parameter and its open/dup2 branch are unreachable; the header comment (process.cpp:42-47) even documents both users as 'stdin inherited'.
findings.safety: Deleting the parameter and the if-block removes only never-executed code; both call sites already take the false path, so child processes get identical fd setups.
findings.verify_with: Rebuild + andesim-run-test (passthrough argv assembly) and a fast/cycle smoke via tests/andes_sim/test_andes_sim_default_run.sh; scripts/run_e2e.sh exercises exec_passthrough end-to-end.

Only the context prefix differs. A small helper (e.g. next to resolve_accurate_engine in engine_registry.hpp, taking the prefix and Discovery) collapses ~30 lines to 3 call sites and keeps the three diagnostics from drifting.

findings.detail: run_process({bin, "--print-qemu-config"}, 5000) is spelled with a literal 5000 at cmd_run.cpp:509-510 (memmap probe) and cmd_profile.cpp:315-316, while run_plan.cpp:109 names the same value kQemuCfgProbeMs in a file-local anonymous namespace (used at run_plan.cpp:399). cmd_run.cpp:511-513 additionally re-implements the probe-validity predicate `!spawn_failed && !timed_out && rc == 0` that stage_qemu_cfg already owns (run_plan.cpp:145). Hoisting kQemuCfgProbeMs into run_plan.hpp (or exposing a probe_qemu_cfg(bin) helper returning the cfg text) makes the three probe sites share one timeout and one predicate.

The implementation (shm.cpp:209-212) builds '[andesim] mmap <size> at <dir> (free: ...)' with ' (fallback: ...)' - different prefix, different fallback separator - and emits it via log_line(kLogDebug), i.e. only when --log-level >= debug, not unconditionally. tests/andes_sim/test_andes_sim_log_level.sh:8 explicitly calls '[hsim mmap]' 'the retired prefix', confirming the header comment predates the rename. findings.title: lm_suffix also carries the L2C MMIO base; name and {plugin_args} comment say 'LM' only
findings.detail: plan_argvs builds a comma-suffix named lm_suffix (run_plan.cpp:253) from ilm_size/dlm_size/hvm_size AND l2c_base (line 257) - the L2C platform-cache MMIO window base, which is not a local memory. The comment describing the composed {plugin_args} (lines 284-286) likewise says 'plus the LM sidecar-drain args', omitting the l2c token. The name predates the shared-cache descriptor work (commit ff583f3). Renaming to e.g. hw_suffix (and amending the comment) restores intent; it is a function-local variable with zero external visibility.

findings.title: Plan-failure repro reporting duplicated between the main hybrid run and the --verify oracle run
findings.detail: run_hybrid prints the same failure block twice: lines 617-627 (main plan: error line, then '[andesim] repro: kept run artifacts at %s (see manifest.txt)', then the log-file hint, return 1) and lines 709-717 (--verify oracle plan: same error+repro lines with prefix 'andesim run --verify:', no log-file hint, return 1). The repro-artifacts message is byte-identical in both. A small local lambda/helper taking (prefix, PlanResult) unifies them and keeps the two copies from drifting; whether the verify copy should also print the log-file hint is a separate (behavioral) question - the structural extraction can preserve the current asymmetry with a flag or by leaving the hint at the first call site.
findings.safety: Extracting the shared lines into a lambda that emits the same strings in the same order changes nothing observable; both sites keep return 1.
findings.verify_with: tests/andes_sim/test_andes_sim_repro.sh (asserts the exact 'kept run artifacts at' line and parses the dir from it).

findings.title: --runtime linux staging block duplicated between run_fast and run_hybrid
findings.detail: run_fast (cmd_run.cpp:209-234) and run_hybrid (cmd_run.cpp:543-550) both: call stage_linux_runtime(app_elf, mem_bytes, cli.passthrough, stage_err), fail with a mode-specific prefix when it returns empty, and log the identical '[andesim] --runtime linux: staged %s (app=%s)' line. Only the error prefix and the mem-bytes derivation differ. Additionally, run_fast's linux path runs check_one_elf + abs_elf twice for the same positional: once at lines 210-213 and again inside run_standalone (lines 143-147) via the cli2 forward - redundant (idempotent) validation work. A helper like stage_linux_boot(app_elf_abs, mem_bytes, passthrough, ctx_prefix, out_err) would collapse both sites and pin the log line in one place.
findings.safety: The staged behavior, message text, and failure exits are identical when the helper reproduces the existing strings; the double check_one_elf/abs_elf is idempotent, so removing the repeat does not change any outcome (same diagnostics, same result path).
findings.verify_with: tests/andes_sim/test_andes_sim_runtime_linux.sh and test_andes_sim_runtime_dual.sh (cover fast and hybrid --runtime linux staging, incl. failure messages).
